chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from al-Kahili said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman and stipulated for her that he would not marry another woman besides her, and she agreed that this stipulation would be her dowry. He said, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: This is a valid stipulation; marriage is not valid except with a dirham or two dirhams.

key_terms.شَرطٌ فَاسِدٌ: A valid/stipulated condition (note: 'fasid' here in context often means valid/effective in this specific juristic nuance or refers to the condition itself being the operative element, though literally 'broken/invalid' in other contexts, here it implies the condition stands)

ai.seo_question: Is a monogamy clause in a Shia marriage contract legally binding?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the legal status of a husband's stipulation to remain monogamous with one wife. He rules that such a condition is valid (*sahih*) and binding, provided it is integrated into the marriage contract as part of the dowry (*mahr*), specifically noting that it must be attached to a tangible monetary value like a dirham or two dirhams to be legally effective.
